abstract: G protein-coupled receptors database (GPCRdb) enables research on GPCRs through tailored resources for reference data, analysis, visualization, experiment design, and dissemination. Our 7th major update to GPCRdb brings extensive updates to the structural and ligand resources, along with several improvements that facilitate easier use. The Structure coverage page has been overhauled to better overview all experimental structures and to break these down into a GPCR class, receptor family, or an individual receptor. We have expanded the annotation on the Structures page by combining AI with manual curation. We add structure models of drug- and peptide-GPCR complexes generated by Boltz-2 and AlphaFold2-Multimer, respectively, and score their confidence. For ligands, we have enhanced the data in the GPCR-ligand interactions resource, implemented variants distinguishing stereoisomers, salts, and labeled versions, assigned persistent identifiers enabling lookup and database cross-linking, and visualized peptide sequences in 2D. Finally, the Data mapper page now has a simplified data input directly in the web interface enabling swift mapping of users' own data for receptors visualized as a GPCRome wheel, tree, clusters, list, or heatmap. Together, these new features aid a multitude of use cases spanning from basic research on GPCR structure-function to drug design. GPCRdb is available at https://gpcrdb.org.
